claims.content: Initiate an Emergency Point Report to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Initiate an Emergency Point Report to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report for an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts, thereby reporting the existence of that condition.
scope_contract.start_boundary: System Operator begins the initiation of the Emergency Point Report for the emergency condition.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Emergency Point Report has been initiated, reporting the existence of the emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.
in_scope_actions: Report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts
excluded_adjacent_actions: Update a previously reported emergency point with additional or more current information
Execute or manage search and rescue efforts
Perform downstream processing of the initiated Emergency Point Report

missing_aspects: Evidence specifying that the 'System Operator' is the exclusive or primary initiator of this report, rather than an automated system function.

claims.content: System Operator
The System Operator has information about the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The System Operator has information about the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts and initiates an Emergency Point Report to report that condition.
The System Operator, through operator action only, initiates an Emergency Point Report to report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.

The Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message that includes the TN(s) assigned by the reporting JU and the position reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values; the reporting JU is the latest JU to report the point and therefore has R² for that point.
Upon receipt of the initiation message, all receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases.
Diverges from Step 1: Any JU may report, through operator action only, on a previously reported emergency point when that JU has additional or more current information on the point.
Diverges from Step 2: When the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the Emergency Point Report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
At Step 1, if the System Operator attempts to initiate an Emergency Point Report for a Reference Point or a Space/Ballistic Missile Track, the Emergency Point Report shall not be initiated.

At Step 2, if Force Tell and Emergency Indicators are set in the J3 message, the message overrides all operator-controllable data filters; as a result, the Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message and all receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases.
The Emergency Point Report has been initiated and transmitted as a J3.1 message, reporting the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
The reported emergency point has been assigned a TN (or TNs) by the reporting JU and its position has been reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
The reporting JU, as the latest JU to report the point, has R² for that point.
All receiving JUs have accepted the emergency alert in their databases upon receipt of the initiation message.

quality_flags.detail: [altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 0 says 'Diverges from Step 1' but describes any JU reporting on a previously reported emergency point with additional/current information. Main flow Step 1 is the System Operator initiating a new Emergency Point Report for an emergency condition. Reporting on a previously reported point is the update action explicitly excluded from this use case, so the divergence point is logically unrelated to Step 1.

inconsistency_hints: Main Flow step 2 only states that the Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message. It does not state or otherwise establish that the report content assigns TN(s) and reports the point using geodetic latitude/longitude, nor that the reporting JU becomes the latest reporter with R². Postconditions 2 and 3 therefore are not reachable from the Main Flow as written.

Exception flow claim 2 says at Step 2, if Force Tell and Emergency Indicators are set in the J3 message, the message overrides all operator-controllable data filters, but it does not state whether the flow returns to a main flow step, terminates, or reaches an explicit terminal failure/prevention state.

Alternative flow claim 0 is encoded with step_number=1, but its text explicitly says 'Diverges from Step 2'. The exercise-indicator branch depends on the J3.1 message, which is part of main_flow Step 2, so the structured attachment point is inconsistent with the stated divergence point.
